proof_summary: Using \(D(n)\equiv n\pmod 9\), the proof exploits eventual periodicity of powers of \(10\) modulo \(D(n)\): starting with \(D(n)\) exponents whose power-sum is divisible by \(D(n)\), it repeatedly replaces one exponent by ten larger ones, preserving divisibility while increasing the number of exponents by nine. This yields a number \(k\) with exactly \(n\) distinct decimal \(1\)-digits, so \(D(k)=n\), \(D(n)\mid k\), and \(k\ge 10n>n\).
